checks.what: certificate from an untrusted (rogue) CA is refused
certificate for the wrong host name is refused
a client without the CA does not trust the server (no verification bypass)
the plain-HTTP upstream (loopback only) is not reachable from another host
client refuses a non-HTTPS remote URL and still fails open (exit 0, nothing queued, nothing sent in clear)
missing and unknown bearer tokens get 401
a credential cannot use another actor's capture registration (404)

scenarios.title: Network interruption, offline operation, bounded buffering, server restart, restoration

checks.what: X4: clients are disconnected from the server network
X5/X6: hooks stay silent, exit 0 and finish inside the 5 s hook timeout while disconnected (fail-open)
X6: events were durably buffered on each client
X6: 1100 concurrent hook invocations all exited 0 while the spool was full (fail-open)
X6: local buffer is bounded at the 1000-entry cap under concurrent writers
X12: client C spool reversed and three envelopes duplicated
X7: server process is really down (loopback upstream refuses)
X7: server process restarted and answers (401 without token)
X7/X8: server restarted while clients were offline; connectivity restored and TLS endpoint answers
X8: both client buffers drain to zero after restoration
X9: every committed event id is unique (no double commits)
X9: each buffered fill event is committed exactly once
X9/X12: duplicated and reordered offline events each appear exactly once
X10: SessionEnd events generated while disconnected were delivered and closed both remote sessions
X10: delivery of those SessionEnd events queued handoff generation on the server (no model was run in this harness)
X12: committed journal verifies after duplicate/reordered/outage delivery
events land only in the credential owner’s workspace
no cross-workspace writes by either actor
no event is attributed to anything but the two credentialed actors

scenarios.title: Replay of already delivered envelopes cannot corrupt committed memory

checks.what: server spool fully committed before replay
replaying three delivered envelopes is accepted by the server but commits nothing new
journal still verifies after replay

scenarios.title: Revoked credentials cannot resume delivery until reauthenticated

checks.what: credential revoked on the server
the revoked token is refused immediately (401)
client keeps working (fail-open) and retains the 3 undeliverable events
draining with the revoked token delivers nothing
the old token still delivers nothing after a new credential exists
with the newly issued credential the retained events are delivered exactly once

scenarios.title: Client process/container crash and restart with events still queued

checks.what: X14: receiver is down while the client keeps queueing
after SIGKILL of the whole client container mid-write, buffered envelopes survive and none is corrupt (stray .tmp files are ignored)
after restart the survivors drain and each is committed exactly once
final committed state is consistent: journal verifies

scenarios.title: Final state consistency after all recoveries

checks.what: unique event ids, verified journal, empty server-side spool

observed: hooks are silent by design (stdout empty, exit 0); the client-visible signal is spool depth; the server exposes committed events, journal verification and its spool stats; the client has no retry timer or backoff — delivery is attempted on each hook and on explicit drain-remote (each attempt bounded to 2 s and 100 files)
NOT_RUN: physical separate hosts, real network paths, iptables DROP (hanging connections), clock skew, packet loss: not reproducible with containers on one machine
